description:
The planning-lead skill, its manifest validator and the plan, breakdown and in-skill review prompts size work in one direction only: every rule splits, and nothing merges, bounds the total or scopes the container. Plans therefore grow with each review round. The b697a3f7 manifest reached 114 issues, 37 of its 107 tasks touched one or two files, and the owner rejected it.

## Background

The terminal rule asks authors to split work until each leaf has one outcome, and it forbids combining foundation, migration, deletion and documentation work. Introducing a form, moving its callers and deleting the old form, which is one change under `@/charter/D-18` and `@/inv/convention-convergence`, therefore becomes a chain of three or four tasks with temporary bridges. All eight validator sizing warnings flag oversize. Warnings are denied, and findings are fixed "by replacing", so splitting is always the cheapest fix. No step checks whether the container itself should become stories, and every task pays a fixed implementation, review and serialized gate cost that no rule weighs.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The terminal rule defines a task as the largest coherent change one worker can implement and review in one focused cycle. Adding a form, moving its callers and deleting the old form within one module, with their docs and tests, is one task.
- [hard] REQ-02: The manifest validator fails a manifest whose issue count exceeds a budget, 50 by default and adjustable by an explicit flag.
- [hard] REQ-03: The validator warns about a terminal that only links a producer-to-remover chain or a bridge pair within one module.
- [hard] REQ-04: Mixing deliverable classes is no longer a sizing warning. Implementation plus release remains one.
- [hard] REQ-05: Before authoring the manifest, the skill scopes the container. A container with many criteria or several unrelated areas is split into stories or separate containers.
- [hard] REQ-06: The in-skill reviewer and both review gates fail a sizing row only when one worker cannot deliver it in one focused cycle, and they also fail over-splitting: chain-link tasks, bridge producer and remover pairs, and an issue count over budget.
- [hard] REQ-07: Review findings are resolved by replacing or merging, and each review round reports the change in issue count.
- [hard] REQ-08: The breakdown skill's sizing text matches the planning-lead terminal rule.
- [hard] REQ-09: The manifest tool's test suite covers the budget failure and the chain-link warning, and it passes.

## Notes

Owner decision recorded during the b697a3f7 restructure: at most 50 issues per manifest, stories included, with one task per coherent in-module change. A prior breakdown-review run failed a leaf solely for combining a cutover with the relocation it required, which shows the over-splitting pressure.


Completion evidence (2026-11-06): merged at e2e50122a. The manifest-tool suite (evals/test-manifest-tool.sh) passes. Full cargo-ci on merged main cca669c5d passed with JIT_AGENT_ID set, which only works around the pre-existing main failure 783b33fa owns; this change does not touch release identity.
title: Planning sizing bounds manifests and merges coherent changes
